_comment: Coverage floors enforced by scripts/check-coverage.ts against the `All files` row of Bun's text coverage reporter. The ratchet only goes UP — raise floors as coverage improves. Lowering a floor means deleting tests, which needs a tracker reference in the diff. The script never auto-edits this file.
_scope: Coverage is scoped to SITE-AUTHORED LOGIC. `bunfig.toml` `coveragePathIgnorePatterns` drops two groups. (1) Presentational Astro output — components, layouts, pages, styles, assets, content, every `.astro` file — plus the generated `.upstream/` checkout: a unit test cannot say anything useful about a template that renders markup, and those files answer to `check:bundle-size` (which also runs the a11y sweep) and Starlight's link validator instead. (2) The eight scripts vendored byte-identically from `templates/l5-toolkit/scripts/` at the os-eco root — check-all, check-ci-parity, check-coverage, check-debt-markers, check-file-sizes, validate-agents-md, report-test-timing, report-quality-metrics. Those are authored and tested in the template repo, two of them are asserted byte-identical by `cmp`, and none of them may be edited here, so measuring them reported the TEMPLATE's coverage under this repo's name and moved the floor away from code this repo can act on. Their `.test.ts` files still run; only the accounting is scoped out. What remains measured: the upstream content pipeline (`sync-upstream.ts`, `upstream/**`), the a11y and bundle-size guards, and the prose guard.
_measured: Floors set from a real measurement with the scope above: functions 87.22%, lines 84.99% (raised from 86.31% / 83.93% when `scripts/upstream/tokens.ts` landed at 100% / 100%). They sit a little under those numbers so ordinary churn does not fail the gate on noise. This is HONEST, not a target — the site is below 90%, and two files are the whole gap. (1) `scripts/sync-upstream.ts` at 14% functions / 19% lines: the deliberately-thin impure shell of the content pipeline — clone, read, write, diff — where every decision it could get wrong already lives in the pure, 100%-covered modules under `scripts/upstream/`. (2) The `main()` and reporting halves of `check-prose.ts`, `check-a11y.ts`, and `check-bundle-size.ts`, which print and exit. Covering either group means driving `git clone`, a real `dist/`, and process exit codes, so the honest way to raise this floor is integration tests over fixtures, NOT unit tests written to move a number.
